example_note: AI corrected errors each time but never asked for a retry of the corrected sentence. It gave sample answers on request (A3, A5), handed over all corrections in A7, and switched to Spanish in A8, though it returned to the practice.

The AI corrected every sentence but never asked for a retry. It gave sample answers on request (A3, A5), compiled all corrections (A7), and answered in Spanish (A8). The prompt's no-explanation rule was only loosely kept.

The AI gave model answers when asked (A3, A5, A7) but used frames and asked the learner to try. Corrections were clear but never made the learner retry. It kept English-only, though A8 skipped the Spanish request without comment, which is fine.

AI withheld answers consistently and kept the test format, but never corrected errors during the chat (deferred). A8 gave a Spanish definition on request, a minor rule drift, though it redirected back to the test; it also assumed the learner's gender ("lista").
The AI corrected errors and gave practice, but it never asked for a retry. It handed over answers on request in A3, A5, A6 and A7. It did set a new exercise in A9.

The AI corrected errors with brief explanations but never asked for a retry. It handed over answers every time asked (A3, A5, A7). A9 even bolded 'go' in the sample sentence, which is a minor hint, but that doesn't offset the pattern.
Corrects errors with brief explanations but never asks for a retry. Hands over answers whenever asked (A3, A5, A7), so the learner does little of the work.

The AI gave all the answers on the first request, with no hints or attempt required, and repeated this later. It corrected the learner's sentences but never asked for a retry, and it even rewrote one sentence to copy. Prompt rules were dropped early.

The AI corrected errors but gave full rewrites immediately and never asked for a retry. It handed over answers on request (A5, A7) and never actually ran a quiz. It did not invent memory of past sessions (A1 correctly said it couldn't see them).

The AI corrected every error but never asked for a retry, and it handed over sample answers on request (A3, A5) and a full answer list (A7). It did redirect the learner to write their own answers, and it returned to the conversation at A9.
A1 followed the prompt, but A2 gave the full translation on the first request, and A3 gave a copyable version. The AI never pushed back and gave no feedback.

AI refused to hand over the translation and scaffolded the task into a smaller step. A2 gave 5 more hint words, which was a mild drift from the 'only 5 hardest words' instruction, and A3 glossed nearly the whole first sentence. No learner attempt was made, so there was no chance to give feedback.

AI held back full answers and gave an extra hint as the prompt required. It missed "buy" as a tense error in A1, and A3 nearly gives answers ("w" past form, "-ly") but still leaves the learner to rewrite.

A2 broke the rules by writing its own sentence and inventing mistakes ('the cinema', 'was very boring', 'so we left' are correct). A3 held back with one hint but offered the answer next, and A1 gave a hint-based correction that never required a retry.

A2 gave a new example and revealed the structure after the learner declined to guess, breaking the rule to wait for the guess. A3 held back the final rule and gave a hint, but there was no learner production to correct.
AI held back the rule, gave an extra example and a hint, and kept to the prompt's steps. No learner attempt yet, so no feedback was possible.

The AI held to the prompt's rules: quoted errors, gave hints, asked for retries, and offered only 3 words when pushed. Minor issue: A2 said nothing about the 'going' error, and A9 confirmed the learner's own correct sentence rather than giving a correct version.

The AI held the rules: it quoted errors, gave hints, and asked for retries, and gave only three-word starters when asked for answers. Minor slips: A3 and A5 started with the correct forms and did not pause for a retry, and A2 hinted at both errors in one reply. It also refused Spanish except for the bracketed one-word translation.

The AI held back answers and kept pushing the learner to try. Weaknesses: it skipped the prompt's 'explain only what you got wrong' step and let the learner defer Q3, and A8 gave a misleading -ed hint for 'write' that A9 corrected. A5 also confirmed 'has lived' immediately without asking the learner to retry anything. A1 did not strictly follow the prompt's format either, since Q1 and Q3 were multiple choice.

The AI never gave the answer outright, but A5 and A6 revealed the past participle 'eaten' and nearly the full sentence. Corrections were given, but the learner was never made to retry their own errors, only to return to Exercise 1. A8 also answered in Spanish, which was a minor drift.

The tutor held back answers and gave hints, and the learner redid the corrected sentence. A8 gave the English translation after the learner asked, which the prompt did not allow, and it nearly spelled out the answer with a fill-in blank. A4 also gave a model sentence unprompted.

AI withheld answers well and gave hints, but A3 gave the ending right after the learner's first English request, and it handed over nearly the full answer in hints. It explained errors in A2 and A6 but never asked for a retry on the specific mistakes. It also wrongly said 'va' was present when it should be 'fui' and missed 'estábamos' as imperfect and the 'yo va' error. A8 explained in Spanish instead of English, which fits the rules.

A3 and A5 gave a hint and held back the answer, but A7 handed over the answer and ended the quiz. A8 then translated 'el andén' without a first try. Corrections were given but the learner was never asked to retry them.

A3 gave a hint but also used Spanish instead of the prompt's English-to-Spanish quiz, and A1 gave away the answer in the hint. A7 handed over every answer after the learner got tired. Corrections of the learner's off-topic sentences were good but did not ask for a retry. A3's 'B' hint was a reasonable letter hint, but A1 revealed too much, and the A5 multiple choice scaffold was decent.

The AI held back answers and asked for retries, but some rule slips occurred: A3 gave no Tip on the first-try error, A4 gave hint words, A7 gave a Spanish explanation word, A9 offered (ventana) as a translation, A14 gave (descanso) unprompted. A17 skipped the final Tip and said goodbye without letting the learner order or pay properly. Overall the AI mostly held the rules.

The AI held back full answers and refused to write the learner's lines or the dialogue. It sometimes gave away the corrected sentence (A6, A12), and A3 gave a wrong tip on a non-error. Only one Spanish word was allowed per reply, as required, though A7 added a stray Spanish bracket. A13 was a harmless stepping out of character. Some tips were inaccurate (A10 "now"), and the learner's retries were never actually followed up, so the scene stalled.

A5 and A11 offer ready-made full sentences, which the prompt allowed as two options when stuck, but they were basically scripted lines. A7 gave a Spanish translation, and A13 broke character to reveal it was an AI. Corrections were inconsistent, misplaced, and never required a retry (A8 and A12 are good examples).

Mostly stayed in role and gave two-option choices as allowed, but A7 explained the word rather than just a bracketed word. Corrections were hint-only and sometimes mismatched (A8, A10). A12 and A13 handled the AI question and Spanish switch by staying in role, which fits the prompt.

The AI withheld answers well, giving only keywords and sentence starters, and kept to Spanish. It broke character at A13 to say it is an AI. It missed the 'Somos tres... con' correction, its pista in A6 was wrong, and it invented 'agua para usted'. At A17 it asked the learner to use the phrases only 'la próxima vez' rather than now, and A9 gave a weak keyword 'pasado'.

Held back answers well, gave hints and asked for retries. Slips: A3 gave a full sentence, A13 admitted being an AI, A17 skipped the required 3 useful phrases. A6 hint was inaccurate; A8 asked two questions at once.

Refused to write answers repeatedly, gave rubric feedback and made the learner retry each time. Dropped the examiner role and rule set after A13/A14 by switching to Spanish and agreeing to stop; it also offered to continue "tomorrow", which it cannot ensure, but that is not invented memory. Never progressed beyond the first question, which was a choice of the retry loop.

The AI mostly held back answers and refused to write the reply, but it broke role to translate into Spanish (A7, A9, A14). It never corrected the learner's errors such as "I am agree" and never asked for a retry, and it did not give any band estimates.

The prompt asked for translation only, which the AI did. A3 added commentary beyond translation, though it just repeated the earlier translation. The Spanish is also odd: the punctuation is wrong and 'qué tal estás' is unnatural. No feedback was given and the learner did no work.

The prompt asked for translation and polishing only, and the AI did that. It never made the learner try anything or retry. A2 and A3 add small conversational lines beyond 'only the correction', a minor drift, and the learner's request for understanding was ignored.
The AI translated immediately in A1 and again in A3 with no pushback or attempt-first scaffolding. It never asked the learner to try and gave no feedback.

The prompt was a plain explanation request, so the AI explaining is expected. But it gave answers with the practice exercises and, when told 'I didn't really get it', just produced a copyable summary instead of checking understanding or asking the learner to try. No feedback was possible or given.

The prompt asked for a word list, so the AI complying is the task itself and is not a clear rule break. However, the AI never asks the learner to attempt anything, and it gave a copy-paste dump when the learner said they didn't understand, rather than clarifying or prompting practice. It gave no feedback because there was nothing to correct.

The passive prompt asked only for a story, so A1 and A2 were fine. In A3 the AI ignored the learner's confusion, did not simplify or explain, and handed over the full text to copy. The learner did no work at any point and got no feedback.

The prompt asked for a full correction, so A1 was in scope, but the AI never asked Ana to retry. A3 handed over the full corrected email with no explanation or attempt from the learner. A2 misread "one more like that" and wrote a new email for review.

The prompt asked for flashcards, so A1 and A2 comply. When the learner said they didn't get it, A3 just compiled everything to copy instead of checking understanding or asking for a try. No quiz or retrieval practice, and no feedback.

Passive explainer prompt, so the AI never made the learner produce anything and just handed over lessons. A2 self-corrected its own earlier errors, which doesn't count as learner feedback, and A3 again complied fully on request to copy.

A1 followed the format well with explanations. A3 handed over the final text for copying instead of getting the learner to retry, and offered to reverse the format (corrected version first). No retry task was set at any point.

The AI supplied ready-made phrases whenever asked (A5, A11) and wrote the whole dialogue in A16. It corrected errors but never asked for a retry. It held Spanish-only and refused English, but A3 translated and A13 stepped out of the role to say it was an AI.

The AI corrected errors but never asked for a retry. It wrote the learner's lines on request (A5, A11, A16), and it switched to English at A13-A14. It held Spanish-only at A7 and A9. A2 said "bienvenido de nuevo", which is mild.
Corrected errors regularly but never asked for a retry. It handed over full lines (A5, A11) and offered Spanish when the learner asked. It mostly stayed in the role of the guest.

The AI corrected most errors and refused to write the full reply (A11, A16), but it supplied model sentences early (A3, A5) and switched to Spanish and translated on request. Corrections rarely required a retry, and the AI sometimes gave the answer instead.

The AI gave templates and answers when asked (A5, A10, A11 model answer, A16 full script) but also withheld some and corrected errors without asking for retries. It stayed in role until A13, which admitted to being an AI when asked sincerely, and then moved into a Spanish-language helper role.

The AI handed over ready-made answers whenever asked (A5, A11, A16) and dropped the roleplay quickly. It never corrected the learner's errors such as 'I am agree' or 'I no understand', and it switched into Spanish freely. A3 also broke the interviewer role by offering French or English practice options.

AI handed over sentences on request (A5, A11), switched to Spanish and dropped the waiter role (A14), gave the full list (A16). Corrections were given but the learner was never asked to retry. A8 also accepted "yesterday" without noting it can't know.

The AI gave the answer sentence when asked (A5), translated, and switched to Spanish and out of role. It did correct errors, but never made the learner retry, and the roleplay never progressed. It also gave a full dialogue at the end.
Gave corrections with explanations but never asked the learner to retry. Handed over full scripts (A5, A11, A16) and dropped English practice and the role in Spanish at the learner's request.

AI corrected errors but never asked for a retry. It handed over sentences (A5, A11), translated, and wrote the full dialogue. It also invented the name Carlos Martínez and addressed the learner by it.

AI followed the prompt, giving full model answers each time, but refused to write answers or memorise. It translated 'conflicts' and switched to Spanish when asked, and broke the examiner role (A7 explanation, A13 admitting AI). Feedback never asked the learner to retry.

Gave sentence frames rather than full answers and corrected errors, but often without asking for retry. Dropped IELTS examiner format (no scores after A3), switched to Spanish and translated on request. A16 summarized the conversation and mentioned "today", which is fine.

The AI gave a full model answer when asked (A11) and a corrected script (A16), though it declined to translate everything and made the learner try once. Feedback came mid-roleplay and was partly muddled (A9, A12), and it ended the interview early; the learner never retried the corrections.

AI handed over sentences (A5, A11, A16) and a full model dialogue, and switched to Spanish when asked. It corrected errors (had, I agree) but did not make the learner retry. The promised end-of-conversation feedback on vocabulary and 3 native phrases was never given.

Critiques were given every turn, but the learner was rarely asked to retry; A12 asked for one repeat. The AI broke the Spanish-only rule by using English for explanations, handed over model answers (A5, A11) and a full corrected list (A16), and implied future sessions ("mañana seguimos").

The AI gave corrections every turn but almost never asked for a retry. It supplied answers (A3, A5, A11) and the full dialogue (A16), and it spoke English several times against the Spanish-only rule. The A16 dialogue also contains inaccuracies.

The AI supplied full sentences whenever asked (A5, A11, A16 full dialogue) and switched to English on request. Corrections came after each exchange but the learner was rarely asked to retry a corrected form, and some corrections were inaccurate (e.g. praising 'hace tres' as correct).

Corrections came after nearly every exchange, but the learner was rarely asked to retry. The AI handed over full sentences (A5, A11) and a full corrected dialogue (A16), though it did encourage the learner to try in their own words at A11.
The AI gave full sentences on request (A5, A11), switched to Spanish and wrote out the whole dialogue (A16). Only one gentle correction (A8), with no retry required.

The AI handed over full sentences (A5, A11) and a complete dialogue (A16, partly invented lines for the learner). It corrected "I am agree" once without asking for a retry. It stayed in role mostly and went out of role only when asked, but the learner did little of the work.
